blind_spots_patched: The baseline dossier missed the H1 FY27 unaudited cash flow statement showing CFO collapsing to Rs 4.73 Cr (14.3% of Rs 33.16 Cr PAT) due to a Rs 23.89 Cr surge in Other Current Assets (to Rs 54.32 Cr) alongside Rs 50.35 Cr in Other Non-Current Assets (capital advances), resulting in -Rs 54.43 Cr H1 FCF and a guided FY27-end gross debt peak of ~Rs 165–170 Cr.

The baseline dossier benchmarked Kross only against trailer-axle and forging peers (Jamna Auto, RKFL, GNA Axles, Happy Forgings) and omitted the entrenched domestic seamless-tube oligopoly Kross must battle to monetize the ~50% non-captive surplus of its 1,20,000 TPA Mill 219 plant in Oil & Gas and general engineering.

The baseline dossier treated the Oct 30, 2026 Rs 63.6 Cr preferential allotment as a simple equity raise without detailing its two-tranche promoter warrant structure, immediate cash shortfall (only Rs 39.75 Cr received upfront vs. ~Rs 110 Cr H2 FY27 capex), and 18-month warrant conversion overhang (~4.65% total dilution to 6.75 Cr shares).
assumptions_changed: WEAKENED: Baseline ch-3 stated Kross is finishing a Rs 167 Cr seamless tube plant with ~40,000 TPA capacity and framed working capital drag purely around FY26 debtor and inventory days.

WEAKENED: Baseline ch-5 cited 60%–65% extrusion utilization with ~80% extruded axles without distinguishing expanded 7,500/month capacity, noted the verbatim Q2 FY27 transcript was unavailable, and did not disclose FY27-end projected gross debt.
CONFIRMED: Baseline ch-4 stated Kross maintains sticky OEM approvals alongside high customer concentration while competing with Jamna Auto and Ramkrishna Forgings in trailer axles.
WEAKENED: Baseline ch-6 audited cash conversion only through FY26 (30.4% 3-year CFO/PAT; -Rs 111 Cr cumulative FCF) without incorporating H1 FY27 unaudited operating cash flow or FY27-end debt peak.
